chunks: My father (peace be upon him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Sinan from Furat ibn Aḥnaf from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Any believer who withholds from a believer something that he needs, while he has the ability to give it, or it is from another person, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will raise him on the Day of Resurrection with a blackened face, his eyes blueish, his hands tied to his neck, and it will be said: 'This is the untrustworthy one who betrayed Allah and His Messenger.' Then he will be ordered to be taken to the Fire.

key_terms.مُسَوَّدًا: Blackened (face as a sign of disgrace)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of withholding help from a fellow believer when one is able to give?
ai.summary: In Thawab al-A'mal, Shaykh al-Saduq highlights this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq to emphasize the spiritual gravity of hoarding resources from fellow believers, framing it as a betrayal of divine trust. The vivid eschatological imagery of a blackened face and bound hands serves as a physical manifestation of inner moral failure, linking the act directly to the concept of 'al-Khain' (the untrustworthy) who is cast into Hellfire.
